doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Discography check: Rosolino date and the Woody Herman session
summary: Brown reads the Rosolino and March 1954 Woody Herman entries; Holman remembers none of the titles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Any comments about the Woody Herman date? It didn‟t seem like that registered.
Are there any titles with that?

Let me scroll down to that. The one following that – again, these dates are coming in right behind each other. Stan Kenton, and then a Frank Rosolino. I‟m still showing some Stan Kenton. Frank Rosolino is the next date. But the recordings of all your tunes that Stan did, that was in March, early March, March 3rd. Then there‟s a Frank Rosolino, but it‟s Stan Kenton Presents Frank. It‟s a sextet, and they‟ve got some of your arrangements on here. Then the next one is the Woody Herman. Woody Herman is March 30th in New York. It‟s only – it‟s one session, four titles, but it‟s the entire orchestra. The four titles are Mess Around, with a vocal track, Castle Rock, Mambo the Most, and Mambo the Utmost. You‟re listed as an arranger.
I don‟t remember any of those titles.
I think the Lord discography is going to have to have a lot of addenda.
You say there‟s another Woody date?
